pl-l2d20c2-d1e108.summary: Asks why they did not unite in paradise: because transgression came soon after woman's creation and they were expelled, or because God had not yet commanded it, and his authority could be awaited where concupiscence did not press; he had not commanded it because he foreknew their fall.
claims: The fall came soon after creation.
God had not yet commanded union.

pl-l2d20c2-d1e111.summary: Concludes that the mode of procreation has been set out.

pl-l2d20c2.summary: Asks why they did not unite in paradise: because transgression followed soon after woman was created and they were expelled, or because God had not yet commanded it, and divine authority could be awaited where concupiscence did not press; God had not commanded it because he foreknew their fall.
claims: The first parents did not unite in paradise.
Their fall came soon after woman's creation.
God had not yet commanded them to unite, foreseeing their fall.
